question: The concept of multiprogramming was introduced in the ____________ generation of computers.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Third**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The concept of **multiprogramming** was introduced in the **third generation** of computers.
 
• **Multiprogramming** allows multiple programs to run concurrently by managing the use of the CPU and other resources.
 
• This was made possible due to advances in hardware and software, including the development of **integrated circuits** and **operating systems** capable of handling multiple tasks at once.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Generation:** These computers used vacuum tubes for circuitry and magnetic drums for memory. They were very large, consumed a lot of power, and were not capable of multiprogramming.
 
• **Second Generation:** Transistors replaced vacuum tubes, making computers smaller, faster, and more energy-efficient. However, they still did not support multiprogramming.
 
• **Third Generation:** Integrated circuits replaced transistors, leading to the development of smaller, more powerful, and more reliable computers. This generation introduced multiprogramming.
 
• **Fourth Generation:** Microprocessors were introduced, further increasing the power and efficiency of computers. Multiprogramming continued to be used and refined in this generation.
